follow_up_questions.question: Is the skin on the backs of your hands or between your fingers affected as well, or is it only the palms?
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Documenting the exact distribution helps distinguish irritant contact dermatitis (often dorsum-predominant) from allergic contact dermatitis, atopic eczema, or palmar psoriasis, thereby refining or challenging the working diagnosis.

follow_up_questions.question: Have you noticed any tiny fluid-filled blisters on your palms or the sides of your fingers?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: Doctor (Turn 19–20): "Any itchiness in your palms?" / Patient: "Yeah, it does get itchy."
follow_up_questions.reasoning: The presence of vesicles points toward dyshidrotic eczema, while their absence favors simple irritant/contact dermatitis; asking tightens the differential.

follow_up_questions.question: Do the cracked areas ever become red, warm, or swollen?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: Patient (Turn 24): "…when I scratched it, yes it has bled sometimes…"
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Evaluating erythema, warmth or swelling screens for secondary bacterial infection or cellulitis, conditions that can mimic or complicate contact dermatitis and alter management.

follow_up_questions.question: When you do wear protective gloves at work, does the rash get better, worse, or stay the same afterward?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: Patient (Turn 30): "…I’m not always very good about wearing gloves…"
follow_up_questions.reasoning: A worsening under gloves raises concern for allergic contact dermatitis to latex or glove powder, while improvement supports irritant dermatitis from cleaning agents.

follow_up_questions.question: During the three days you were off work, did your hand symptoms improve, worsen, or stay the same?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: Patient (Turn 78): "…the past three days, I haven’t been able to go to work."
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Symptom change when away from exposure is a key feature to confirm occupational contact dermatitis and helps rule out endogenous dermatoses that persist irrespective of work.

follow_up_questions.question: Did you ever have eczema, hay fever, or asthma earlier in life?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: Doctor (Turn 57–60): "Eczema, dermatitis, for example?" / Patient: "Not that I know of."
follow_up_questions.reasoning: A personal atopic history increases the likelihood of endogenous hand eczema and helps differentiate it from purely irritant contact dermatitis.

follow_up_questions.question: Can you recall the names or types of cleaning chemicals you handle most often without gloves?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: Patient (Turn 76): "Yeah, I usually use those for bathrooms…"
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Identifying specific agents guides avoidance advice and, if needed, future patch-testing for allergic contact dermatitis, strengthening causal attribution.

follow_up_questions.question: Are both hands affected equally, or is one hand noticeably worse than the other?
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Unilateral or dominant-hand predominance supports irritant contact dermatitis, whereas symmetric involvement may suggest endogenous eczema or systemic causes, sharpening diagnostic confidence.
